newsitem.title: GERMANY: Jochimsen - Germany hard-pressed on EMU budget goal.
newsitem.headline: Jochimsen - Germany hard-pressed on EMU budget goal.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen said on Friday that Germany will have a difficult time meeting the Maastricht Treaty budget deficit target and that it will be almost impossible to hit the debt targets.
Speaking before an academic group, Jochimsen added that the stability pact designed to ensure fiscal discipline after the launch of monetary union was at risk from less stability-minded nations.
"It is becoming ever more apparent that it will be difficult to meet the budget deficit criteria and almost impossible to meet those on the level of national debt," Jochimsen said.
"It has even become hard to take advantage of the room for interpretation left in the (Maastricht) treaty," he said.
The Maastricht Treaty sets thresholds for deficits of three percent of gross domestic product and calls for states to hold debt levels at or below 60 percent of GDP.
Jochimsen expressed concern about French commitment to a stable euro.
"There is a growing view that France is unwilling and unable" to respect the long term sustainability required for monetary union.
Jochimsen added the European Union summit in Amsterdam to approve the stability pact had hurt the deal by also putting emphasis on job growth.
Calling the Amsterdam summit, a "patchwork or ragbag of amendments," Jochimsen said: "Thus it places the entire project in the balance".

Jochimsen echoed former European Commision President Jacques Delors in calling EMU a social experiment, adding: "Given the unaired tensions and still inadequate political and economic foundations, this may do more harm than good to the continuing process of integration in the whole of Europe."
Departing from his prepared text, Jochimsen said this could lead "to the potential disaster of disintegration."
